title: Fixed survey effort lowered early and raised late median latitude slopes for 63 Northeast US fall taxa in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested how survey effort affects marine latitude trends in two regions and two periods. We held strata and taxon sets fixed in OceanAdapt catch records from 1982-2019. We compared catch-weighted latitude with latitude weighted to a fixed mean effort in each stratum. For 63 Northeast US fall taxa, the median paired slope change was -1.89 km per decade in 1982-1999 and +2.87 in 2000-2019. Four-test bootstrap intervals were -3.94 to -0.30 and +0.24 to +6.02. For 78 eastern Bering Sea taxa, both intervals included zero. Northeast signs held under two further block lengths and an early-period effort reference. These results concern changes between estimators of the same catches. They do not establish an error in the area-weighted OceanAdapt indicator or a climate cause. Missing hauls, catchability, selected taxa, within-stratum sampling and short time series limit inference. The package gives code, derived evidence, source hashes, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Latitude slope estimates from fixed strata and taxa in two survey regions and two periods. Left: median paired slope changes with approximate four-test block bootstrap intervals. Right: separate median slopes under three estimators. Positive values point north.
